rows.n: baseline
rows.b: A simple reference model or score that a new approach must beat to prove it is worth anything.

rows.n: batch
rows.b: A group of examples processed together in one training step, balancing speed against memory.

rows.n: batch inference
rows.b: Processing many requests together in one go to use the hardware efficiently.

rows.n: beam search
rows.b: Keeping several candidate sequences alive and expanding the best ones, trading speed for higher-quality output.

rows.n: benchmark
rows.b: A standard test suite the whole field runs so models can be compared on equal footing.

rows.n: benchmark data
rows.b: Standardized test sets the whole field uses to compare models fairly.

rows.n: BF16

rows.n: bias
rows.b: A learned offset added after a weighted sum, giving each neuron its own starting push.

rows.n: BLEU
rows.b: A classic translation score based on how many word sequences the output shares with reference translations.

rows.n: BOS token
rows.b: The special beginning-of-sequence token marking where a text starts.

rows.n: browser inference

rows.n: byte fallback
rows.b: Representing unknown characters as raw bytes so the tokenizer never truly fails on odd text.

rows.n: byte-pair encoding
rows.b: A tokenizer algorithm that starts from single characters and repeatedly merges the most common pair, building the vocabulary bottom-up.
